chunks: Most exalted of position, Lord of power, He directs inspiration by His command to any of His creatures as He will, to warn (men) of the Day of Meeting,

key_terms.الرُّوحَ: The Spirit (often referring to Gabriel or divine inspiration)

ai.seo_question: Who is Allah described as in Surah Ghafir, and what is the purpose of sending the Spirit?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the divine prerogate of selecting prophets and imams as recipients of the Ruh (often interpreted as revelation or the Holy Spirit), underscoring their role as warners of the Day of Meeting. The mention of 'Lord of the Throne' (Dhu al-Arsh) emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty, while the 'Day of Meeting' serves as a pivotal eschatological concept in Shia theology, marking the final accountability where all secrets are revealed. This selection process is not arbitrary but reflects divine wisdom in choosing those best suited to convey the message to humanity.
